standard_prerequisites.name: Avoidance of finitely many primes by an ideal not contained in them
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the correcting element g in J outside the selected primes.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where there are no inclusion relations among the primes by discarding the smaller ones, and choose an arbitrary lift f of the given class (proof lines 9070-9072).
Let S be the set of indices s with f in p_s; if S is empty the chosen lift already works (proof lines 9072-9073).

Form the ideal J = I times the product of the p_i with i not in S and check that J is not contained in p_s for s in S, because there are no inclusions among the primes and I is contained in none of them (proof lines 9074-9077).
Apply the avoidance lemma to find g in J outside every p_s with s in S, and conclude that f + g is the required lift (proof lines 9078-9080).
proof_roadmap: Remove redundant primes and pick a first lift.
Detect the primes containing the lift.
Build an ideal that avoids exactly those primes.
Correct the lift by an element of that ideal.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an ideal I of a ring A and finitely many primes p_1, ..., p_r none of which contains I, every element of A/I lifts to an element of A avoiding all the p_i. The proof first removes inclusion relations among the primes, picks an arbitrary lift f, and lets S be the set of indices with f in p_s. If S is nonempty it forms the ideal J = I times the product of the p_i with i not in S, verifies that J is not contained in any p_s for s in S (using that there are no inclusions among the primes and that I is in none of them), invokes the avoidance lemma to find g in J outside all the p_s with s in S, and produces the solution f + g (proof lines 9069-9080). H2: the construction of the auxiliary ideal J and the avoidance step are the substance.
